202: And the Lord said to Moses, "Say to Aaron: Take your rod and hold out your arm over the waters of Egypt — its rivers, its canals, its ponds, and all its bodies of water — that they may turn to blood, etc.". Rabbi Yehudah said: One must look into this verse. And how was he able to walk to all of these places? Moreover, it is written: And seven days were completed, after the Lord had smitten the Nile (Exodus 7:25). It writes, "the Nile," and you say, "over the waters of Egypt — its rivers, its canals, and its ponds?"

Rather, "the waters of Egypt" are the Nile. And the waters of all of those other ponds, canals, rivers, and all of its waters were filled from there. And that is why Aaron only held out his arm to strike the Nile alone. Come see that it is so. As it is written: and the Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile (Exodus 7:21).

Come and see! He struck the lowest of all the levels first. Rabbi Shimon said: The Holy One, blessed be He, began from below, and His hand struck with every single finger. But when He reached the highest of all the levels, He did it Himself and passed through the land of Egypt and killed all [the firstborn]. And because of this, He killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt — because it was the highest level and the firstborn of everything.
